question: Is X-linked hyper IgM syndrome inherited ?
references: This condition is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. The gene associated with this condition is located on the X chromosome, which is one of the two sex chromosomes. In males (who have only one X chromosome), one altered copy of the gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the condition. In females (who have two X chromosomes), a mutation would have to occur in both copies of the gene to cause the disorder. Because it is unlikely that females will have two altered copies of this gene, males are affected by X-linked recessive disorders much more frequently than females. A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons.

Yes, X-linked hyper IgM syndrome is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. This means that the gene responsible for the condition is located on the X chromosome. 

In females, who have two X chromosomes, a mutation in one of the X chromosomes can be compensated for by the normal gene on the other X chromosome. However, in males, who have only one X chromosome, a mutation in the gene can lead to the condition because they do not have a second X chromosome to compensate for the mutation.

X-linked hyper IgM syndrome is caused by mutations in the CD40 ligand (CD40L) gene, which is located on the X chromosome. The CD40L gene provides instructions for making a protein that is involved in the activation of B cells, which are a type of immune system cell that produces antibodies. Without a functional CD40L protein, B cells are unable to mature and produce antibodies, leading to the characteristic features of X-linked hyper IgM syndrome, including low levels of IgG and IgA antibodies and elevated levels of IgM antibodies.
